title: On the Swapping Capacity of a Quantum Repeater
authors: Van Sy Mai, Richard J. La, Abdella Battou, Abderrahim Amlou, Cory Nunn
abstract: We study the capacity of a memory-based quantum repeater in entanglement swapping between two quantum links with either single or multiple memories, which we refer to as the end-to-end (E2E) entanglement throughput, subject to a constraint on the minimum fidelity. In order to approximate the E2E entanglement throughput, we adopt queueing models, where quantum links can have different characteristics: memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates and success probabilities, as well as classical communication latencies. We develop a model for estimating E2E entanglement fidelity, while taking into account the heterogeneous dephasing and depolarizing dynamics of quantum memories and Bell-state measurements in entanglement swapping as well as classical communication delays and noises. Finally, with the help of our models for approximating the E2E entanglement throughput and fidelity, we use the maximum waiting times of entanglements in quantum memories at the repeater as optimization variables to maximize the E2E entanglement throughput while ensuring required minimum E2E fidelity.
summary: This paper develops queueing models to analyze the capacity of memory-based quantum repeaters, balancing the trade-off between high entanglement throughput and maintaining a minimum required fidelity. By incorporating detailed noise dynamics from quantum memories and Bell State Measurements, the authors show that optimizing the maximum waiting times in these memories is key to maximizing usable network performance.
main_problem: The study focuses on optimizing the End-to-End (E2E) entanglement throughput of a memory-based quantum repeater while satisfying a minimum required fidelity constraint.
main_result: Optimal performance requires treating the maximum waiting times in quantum memories as optimization variables, leading to model-derived optimal holding times that significantly boost achievable throughput compared to unconstrained scenarios.
method: The authors employ queueing models and stochastic process theory (e.g., CTMC) to approximate the system's rate dynamics under decoherence constraints.
model_or_system: The model describes a quantum repeater network with two links, utilizing quantum memories subject to dephasing and depolarizing noise during entanglement swapping operations.
key_observables: E2E entanglement throughput (rate), average E2E fidelity ($F_{	ext{req}}$).
important_parameters: Memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates, classical communication latencies, and the maximum waiting times (MHTs) in quantum memories.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes independent Poisson generation of elementary entanglements and models decoherence using time-dependent depolarizing/dephasing channels; it does not consider entanglement purification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the timeline of entanglement attempts, show the throughput vs. fidelity trade-off curve, and compare performance when optimal model-based MHTs are enforced versus when they are ignored.
paper_structure: The paper develops queueing models to approximate E2E throughput, derives an expression for E2E fidelity accounting for memory noise and BSM errors, formulates the problem as maximizing rate subject to fidelity constraints, and validates this using simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework connecting resource management (memory time limits) directly to performance metrics (rate vs. fidelity), which is crucial for designing practical quantum communication networks.
